source.title: Emergent Misalignment Recruits a Pre-existing Persona Subspace

page_placements.theme: Latent or margin-level changes can outlast or diverge from behavioral EM

record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes on the insecure-code and educational-code datasets, evaluates broad free-form misalignment, and reports matched-control results; it also tests related narrow fine-tunes and representation interventions.
record.gate_note: The study's own free-generation results for insecure versus educational code are recorded separately by seed and checkpoint. The paper also reports first-step margin routing and training-time forecasts, which are teacher-forced margin measurements rather than free-form answer rates; the first-step contrast is recorded under fits_no_version. Cited results from other papers are not included as rows. Other analyses, including loss geometry and domain-count schedule/order controls, are omitted where they do not directly measure a listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct on the Betley insecure and educational code sets and judges free answers on the 8 canonical questions with the same two-axis gate. It also judges free-form misalignment after medical, financial and sports fine-tunes, and runs activation hold-out and injection interventions read as judged misalignment rates. The judge is a local Qwen2.5-72B, not GPT-4o, and adaptation is LoRA.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that narrow fine-tuning recruits a low-rank persona subspace already present in the frozen instruction-tuned model. Holding it out of activations during fine-tuning prevents broad misalignment (27.7%→0%) and injecting it induces misalignment (to 45.4%), while the same projection on the weight gradient and post-hoc weight edits are inert. The insecure-vs-educational intent contrast is small but reliable at the first-step gradient margin, yet absent or reversed in judged free generations at 14B. Spreading bad data across domains is superadditive in margin transport. All results come from one 14B model with LoRA, and the preventive projection also abolishes the narrow trained behaviour.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the insecure-code and educational-code datasets and framing from Betley et al. (2025) with Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct and a reproduced LoRA recipe, but uses a locally served Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct judge rather than GPT-4o and adds margin-based and subspace interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Judged rates depend on evaluation battery and aggregation: the canonical code battery does not separate insecure from educational training, while the domain-count measurement uses another battery and prompt-unit intervals. Injection rate drops beyond α = 0.30 because coherence collapses. Activation projection and weight-gradient projection give different results; the projection also eliminates narrow adherence.

fits_no_version.finding: The first Adam step on insecure code raises a teacher-forced misalignment margin more than the same code framed as educational (+1.297e6, 69% of clusters positive). Judged rates do not show this ordering.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-data intent tilts the first-step gradient toward broad misalignment on identical tokens, at the margin level.

fits_no_version.finding: Contrastive persona subspaces from the frozen model overlap across 4 domains at 0.513 vs a null of 0.00078. About 82% of the shared core lies outside a style core.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A shared cross-domain persona subspace exists in the aligned model before any misalignment fine-tune.

fits_no_version.finding: Spreading a fixed bad-data budget over 4 domains yields +12.6 nats of transport above a mechanical merge, and +13.0 above a benign mixture. Judged rates do not resolve the domain-count ordering: code+finance is 0.410 vs four-domain 0.269.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Domain-count superadditivity of broad-misalignment transport (margin-based), separate from whether narrow fine-tunes cause misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: An inoculation-style framing lowers first-step routing toward misalignment vs a scrambled placebo (ΔR1 −1.48e6). Endpoint free-form rates were not measured.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inoculation framing reduces the initial gradient coupling to broad misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Constraining the shared write core during fine-tuning lowers the broad margin (−0.541 vs −0.149 random). The judged rate moves 0.226→0.209, with no judged random control. The in-character margin drops from 9.31 to 3.50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A weight-subspace training constraint modestly reduces broad misalignment at a capability cost.

record.problems: All experiments use one model family at 14B. The study itself reports that judged free-generation rates do not distinguish insecure from educational code and are low on the canonical battery. The activation projection removes narrow-task adherence, and the authors state that this does not establish a misalignment-specific capability effect. Its random activation control is one random-subspace draw and is rank-matched but not usage-matched. Several domain-count judged intervals use a prompt-unit approximation because per-generation judgments were not retained.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining domain-count schedule/order-control legs and their rates in Table 61 are not included; they do not add a distinct test of the listed versions beyond the reported domain conditions and mixture control. Detailed first-step forecasts, geometry/curvature results, and post-hoc weight-edit margins are not rows for the listed free-form behavior versions. External studies discussed or cited in the paper are excluded.

untested.parts: Other models and sizes; GPT-4o judge; the 48-question battery as a separate judged rate; the secure-code control's judged rate (secure code appears only in first-step margins).
Reward hacks and number sequences; judged rates for benign single-domain twins.
Mediation in the insecure-code fine-tune (hold-out was run on financial and sports organisms only); other models; whether one direction, rather than a rank-4 per-layer subspace, suffices.

No judged-rate test of inoculation: the inoculation framing is read only as a first-step routing margin, and endpoint confirmation was not run. Brief benign re-training is not tested; the schedule/order legs in Table 61 are not described well enough to read as such.
Model-size comparison; other open models; per-seed rates for the domain organisms; onset before a quarter epoch.

missing.what: Hold-out robustness arms: sports organism unedited 25.9% vs hold-out 0.0%; two-epoch unedited 25.3% vs hold-out 0.024%; single-direction organism with carrier removed 0.0% over 2800 responses.
Writer gradient kept parallel to the carrier: 11.5% vs unfiltered 26.7%, narrow adherence 0.507.
Published Turner organisms judged by this study: medicine 0.0667, finance 0.2917, sports 0.175 (short sample); published financial organism unmodified 27.9%.
Aggregation sensitivity of judged rates: the same baseline reads 0.277 (cluster) vs 0.230 (response); the same injection reads 0.454/0.504/0.583 under three conventions.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V6 challenge was dropped: the educational-code arm is the original paper's own V1 control (insecure code requested for a class), not an inoculation-prompt test. A reader who treats educational framing as inoculation would instead read those rows as challenging V6 at 14B. Table 61's schedule/order legs ('bad then benign' 0.1955, 'benign then bad' 0.2164, 'benign last' 0.0000) might bear on V6's benign re-training, but the paper does not describe them; rows_left_out dismisses them too quickly. The judge is AWQ Qwen2.5-72B, and its scores are quantized onto about 10 values. Batteries differ across campaigns, so rates are not comparable across tables. Three of the 8 canonical questions never elicit a gated response.

versions.untested_parts: The study evaluates insecure and educational code on Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, but does not test all versions of the original training setup, models, or evaluation judges.
It tests narrow fine-tunes involving medical, financial, sports, and code data, but not reward hacks or number sequences.
No narrow in-context-only condition is tested.
The study tests a rank-4/rank-8 persona subspace and selected causal interventions, not whether one individual linear direction mediates every fine-tune or model.

Educationally framed code is evaluated at trained checkpoints. The inoculation-style reframing is measured at the first-step margin only; endpoint free-generation confirmation is explicitly not run. No brief benign retraining intervention is tested.
The study uses one 14B model, with seed comparisons in the code experiment and a coherence gate. It does not compare model sizes or establish robustness across open models.
